questions.question: What converts p→q to q→p?
What converts p→q to ¬p→¬q?
What converts p→q to ¬q→¬p?
What is true when at least one disjunct is true?
What is true when exactly one disjunct is true?
What principle states p∨¬p is always true?
questions.explanation: Every proposition is true or false.

questions.question: What form contains only conjunctions of literals?
What form contains only disjunctions of literals?
What are propositional variables also called?
questions.explanation: Atomic formulas are basic building blocks.

questions.question: What method checks logical equivalence?
In conjunctive normal form, what is each disjunction of literals called?
questions.explanation: A CNF formula is a conjunction of clauses, where each clause is an OR of literals.

questions.question: Name a single binary connective that is functionally complete on its own.
questions.explanation: NAND (and likewise NOR) alone can express NOT, AND, and OR, hence all connectives.

questions.question: What is the simplest equivalent form of (p∨q)∧(p∨¬q)?
The tautology ((p→q)∧p)→q expresses which rule of inference?
questions.explanation: From p→q and p we infer q — the schema of modus ponens.

questions.question: How many rows does the truth table of a proposition with 5 variables have?
A SAT solver runs unit propagation on the clause set (¬p∨q), (p), (¬q∨r). Starting from the unit clause (p), what final assignment is forced?
alternatives: p, q, and r all true
questions.explanation: p=T makes (¬p∨q) unit, forcing q=T; that makes (¬q∨r) unit, forcing r=T.

questions.question: How many satisfying assignments does (p∨q)∧(¬p∨q)∧(p∨¬q)∧(¬p∨¬q) have?
questions.explanation: The four clauses rule out FF, TF, FT, and TT respectively — every assignment falsifies a clause, so the formula is unsatisfiable.

questions.question: Convert p→(q∧r) to conjunctive normal form.
Give a satisfying assignment for the formula (p→q)→p.
questions.explanation: With p=T the outer consequent is true regardless of q; with p=F the antecedent p→q is true while p is false, making the whole formula false.

questions.question: Under the assignment p=True, q=False, r=True, evaluate ((p→q)∨(r∧¬q))↔p.
questions.explanation: p→q = T→F = F, but r∧¬q = T∧T = T, so the disjunction is T; T↔T = T.
